# 3 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** The Royal Decree Against the Jews

---

**1** When Ptolemy learned all of this, and found out that the Jews were firmly resolved and would not submit to his decrees, having also heard that some were favorable toward him and many completely devoted to him, he gave orders to leave them exactly as they were, to hold them under armed guard, bound in iron chains on all sides, and to provide them with no help or comfort whatsoever.

**2** By royal decree they were stripped of all their property and civil rights.

**3** They were not even allowed to draw water from wells or receive any of the necessities of life.

**4** All this was accomplished through royal decrees, as is typical of a king without reason or wisdom.

**5** But word of their situation reached the Jews' friends, since many Alexandrians had close ties with them, and these friends visited them secretly, bringing food and offering encouragement.

**6** This lifted the Jews' spirits with hope, and the Alexandrians also pledged to do everything in their power to get them released.

**7** Ptolemy then issued additional orders, commanding that the entire Jewish population be gathered in one place and brought to him under guard.

**8** He also commanded that anyone of status who refused to comply with his orders concerning the Jews, or who tried to help them in any way, should be put to death.

**9** After these measures were carried out and great violence had been done to the Jews, a strong desire arose among all the people of Judea to stand with the Jews and come to their aid.

**10** Then the king, puffed up with arrogance and drunk on his own power, sent the following letter.

**11** King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders and soldiers throughout Egypt and all its territories, greetings. I am well and my affairs are going smoothly.

**12** Since the Asian campaign has ended as we wished and we have returned safely by the grace of the gods, we have now resolved, not by force but by benevolence, to attend to the service of the local gods.

**13** However, the Jews continue to show hostility toward us, refusing to submit to our authority, treating our sacred sites with contempt, and stirring up unrest in our kingdom.

**14** We have therefore resolved to deal with them accordingly and to make them publicly answer for their insolent behavior.

**15** Our instructions to you are as follows: all the Jews in your area are to be arrested and transported to Alexandria, brought to us under guard.

**16** They are to receive absolutely no compassion or mercy.

**17** We are confident that these enemies of our rule have been overcome and that our authority over them is total.

**18** On their arrival in Alexandria they are to be executed by torture.

**19** In this way we will rid ourselves of this entire people.

**20** All their property is to be seized for the royal treasury.

**21** Anyone who shelters a Jew will be put to death.

**22** We are distributing copies of this letter throughout the land so that it will be known to all and so that everyone will be ready to carry out our command without fail or exception.
